notes:
Pass-1 sprint-owner seat taken by claude-fable-5 in the operator-launched interactive console. Running log: docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass1/OWNER-LOG.md (decisions D1-D6). Three findings of evidentiary value for the pass itself, all from 2026-08-20 evening.

FINDING 1 — tools/runner crashed unhandled at the exact call site pass 1 replaces. When the tournament's qwen lane was killed under host memory pressure (20:20 local), tools/runner:1505 raised PermissionError [Errno 1] from os.killpg and the runner died with a traceback (trailer: /private/tmp/weizigo/pass1-tournament/untracked/bakeoff/pass1-spec-tournament/qwen3.8:27b-mlx/trailer.log). The seed brief cites runner:1505 as the killpg site the new managent ownership verb replaces; it failed in production on tournament day. EPERM from killpg is itself evidence for the measured escape mechanism (group members in other sessions / already-reaped leaders). Feed to consolidation (ladder phase 2/3).

FINDING 2 — keeper double-dispatch of an operator-launched seat. The fleet keeper dispatched kanban row T554 headlessly at 20:25:51 local (bin/subagent --provider claude --model claude-fable-5 T554 --wall=2700; keeper pressure file listed T554 as its running row) BEFORE the cooldown file landed at 20:28:56, while the operator was launching the same row by hand in an interactive console — which the T554 brief defines as the seat. Result: two owners racing the same deliverables; the duplicate dispatched its own seven graders 30 s after the console's. Duplicate tree (3 pids) enumerated by ppid-walk and SIGKILLed ~20:45; no orphans, no repo damage; its logs left at untracked/T554-grader-logs/ and untracked/runs/T554.json. Generalization of the T541 finding: the keeper has no notion of preconditions, and additionally no notion of a seat the operator is hand-launching. Candidate owning rows: T496/T511 (keeper duty / single-instance).

FINDING 3 — the runner's per-instance host-memory floor turns one memory hog into a fleet-wide massacre recorded as per-lane failures. Grading attempt 1 ran 14 lanes (7 mine + 7 duplicate's) while the qwen3.8:27b-mlx MLX model (~15 GB resident) loaded; host avail fell below the 6144 MB floor and EVERY tools/runner instance independently killed its own lane at ~116-120 s (trailer readings 4.8-6.1 GB), i.e. 14 culls attributed to lanes that did nothing wrong. This reproduces on the grading instrument the seed brief's defect ('a guard culled 12 workers, culls recorded as model failures'). Evidence: untracked/bakeoff/pass1-grading-round1/attempt1-massacre/. Remedy applied (OWNER-LOG D6): qwen removed from the parallel set and run solo; MANAGENT_TASK_ID exported so heartbeats attribute. Grading-round validity note: attempt-1 lane deaths are harness kills, not model readings — no model may be graded down on them.

GRADING-ROUND RECORD KEEPING: tournament closed at 6 of 7 lanes (qwen 0 bytes, reason = FINDING 1 kill); anon set is 8 documents (6 specs + null near-duplicate + seeded weak control); sealed key relocated out of graders' reach to the owner's session scratchpad with sha256 unchanged (6ce50e8f4c559bdb0ab88e055835e32bb2a6cd1322d2dd1b256fa49cb11c50e5, commitment at docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S01-process-ownership/pass1/grading/key.sha256) — OWNER-LOG D1. Grader brief = T553 ruling verbatim with three recorded mechanical adaptations (8 docs not 9; stdout capture deposited by owner instead of grader file-writes; size-range sentence reworded to avoid fingerprinting the seeded control) — OWNER-LOG D3. All six surviving tournament lanes self-identified despite 'Do not name yourself' (flagged in lanes.json, redacted in out.sanitized.md): uniform across models, separates nobody, recorded as a data point per T553.
